# Context Reader

> A free, open-source Chrome extension that explains a hard word using the sentence around
> it, in 13 languages. It calls the Google Gemini API directly from the user's browser with
> the user's own API key. There is no backend server, no analytics and no account.

## What it does

A reader selects a word on any web page. The extension sends that word plus its surrounding
sentence to Gemini and returns the sense that fits the context — not a dictionary list of
every possible meaning. If the word is already in the reader's chosen language it is
simplified rather than translated.

## Distinguishing facts

- **No server.** The extension holds exactly one host permission,
  `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/*`, enforced by Chrome. Nothing belonging to
  the project sits between the user and Google.
- **Bring your own key.** The user supplies a free Gemini API key, stored in
  `chrome.storage.local` and optionally encrypted at rest with AES-GCM behind a passphrase.
- **No telemetry of any kind.** No analytics, no crash reporting, no identifiers.
- **Tuned vs. community languages.** English and Sinhala ship contrastive worked examples
  checked by a speaker, which measurably improve domain-correct sense selection. The other
  eleven languages work without them and the interface labels them as such rather than
  implying parity.

## Languages

English and Sinhala (tuned); Tamil, Hindi, Arabic, Chinese (Simplified), Japanese, Korean,
Russian, Spanish, French, Portuguese, German.

## Licence

MIT. Bundled third-party code (Mozilla Readability, PDF.js, a Sinhala Unicode converter,
pdfium) retains its own licences; see NOTICE in the repository.
